### Executive Summary
- Active exploitation confirmed for a new Chrome V8 zero-day (CVE-2026-85046) and for Sangoma Switchvox (CVE-2026-9586); both are “patch fast / detect now” items.
- Public PoC now available for a **critical unauthenticated JetBrains TeamCity RCE** (CVE-2026-63077); treat any exposed TeamCity as high-risk.
- Multiple “internet-facing edge / tooling” exploit signals (SonicWall SMA SSRF PoC, WordPress arbitrary upload RCE PoC, AWS bulletins affecting open-source tooling) increase likelihood of opportunistic scanning and initial access attempts.

---

### High-priority items (immediate attention)

**1) Chrome / Chromium V8 zero-day actively exploited (CVE-2026-85046)**
- **What happened:** Google shipped an emergency Chrome update for an in-the-wild exploited V8 type confusion (CVE-2026-85046); CISA added it to KEV.
- **Why it matters operationally:** High-likelihood endpoint compromise via drive-by/web content; often pairs with follow-on payload delivery and credential theft.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Verify fleet is on **Chrome 152.0.7977.82/.83+** (or managed equivalent) and enforce auto-update; prioritize investigations of recent “browser spawned” process trees and unusual download/execution events.

**2) Sangoma Switchvox exploited in the wild (CVE-2026-9586)**
- **What happened:** Unauthenticated SQLi in Switchvox is being exploited, reportedly leading to remote code execution.
- **Why it matters operationally:** VoIP/admin appliances are frequently internet-facing; compromise can enable credential access, call fraud, pivoting into internal networks.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Identify any Switchvox exposure (external scan + CMDB) and confirm patch/hotfix status; hunt for abnormal web requests to Switchvox interfaces and any new admin users/config changes.

**3) JetBrains TeamCity critical unauthenticated RCE PoC (CVE-2026-63077)**
- **What happened:** A fully functional PoC was released for CVE-2026-63077 (deserialization) enabling unauthenticated RCE; item notes “actively exploited” (treat as probable even if not independently confirmed here).
- **Why it matters operationally:** CI/CD compromise is a direct path to source code, secrets, build pipelines, and downstream supply-chain impact—high value in financial environments.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Locate TeamCity instances (on-prem/cloud), confirm not internet-exposed, and expedite patching/mitigations; review TeamCity server logs for suspicious unauthenticated endpoints, new tokens, new build steps, or sudden agent registrations.

**4) Edge/perimeter & web platform PoCs gaining traction (SonicWall SMA SSRF, WordPress RCE/upload)**
- **What happened:** PoCs published for SonicWall SMA8200V SSRF chain (CVE-2026-83548/83549, CVSS 10) and a WordPress cookie-consent plugin unauthenticated file upload → RCE (CVE-2026-75865); additional WP plugin account takeover tooling also surfaced.
- **Why it matters operationally:** These are commonly mass-scanned targets; if any are present in DMZ/marketing environments, compromise can become a beachhead for phishing, brand abuse, or internal pivoting.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Ask infra/web teams to confirm whether SonicWall SMA and the referenced WP plugins exist anywhere (including subsidiaries/brand sites); temporarily tighten WAF/IPS rules and block unexpected admin paths/uploads while patching/validation is underway.

**5) AWS security bulletins for tooling used in cloud/dev workflows (postgres-mcp-server, log4j hotpatch tool)**
- **What happened:** AWS published bulletins for CVE-2026-85787 (awslabs postgres-mcp-server SQL validation bypass leading to out-of-scope data modification) and CVE-2026-85656 (command injection in an AWS log4j hotpatch tool).
- **Why it matters operationally:** These impact developer/automation components; exploitation could alter data, implant CI/CD backdoors, or tamper with production telemetry/response tooling.
- **Recommended immediate actions for the SOC today:** Inventory whether these components are used in any internal repos/AMIs/containers and flag to platform engineering for immediate upgrade; monitor for unusual changes to DB content “read-only” workflows and unexpected shell execution from utility hosts.

---

### Monitoring & detection recommendations
- **Chrome zero-day follow-on behaviors:** EDR telemetry for browser child processes (chrome.exe/Chromium) spawning scripting/rundll32/powershell/mshta (T1203, T1059); correlate with web proxy download logs and Mark-of-the-Web events.
- **Switchvox exploitation signals:** WAF/reverse-proxy + appliance HTTP logs for SQLi patterns and unauthenticated access to admin endpoints (T1190); watch for new user creation, config exports, and any outbound connections from the appliance.
- **TeamCity compromise/hardening hunts:** TeamCity application logs + host EDR for new services, unusual `java` child processes, suspicious build step additions, and credential/secret access attempts (T1190, T1552); alert on new agent registrations from unexpected IP ranges.
- **Perimeter scanning / exploit attempts:** Firewall/IDS/IPS for spikes in inbound requests to VPN/web management ports and known appliance paths (SonicWall SMA web endpoints) (T1595); add rate-based alerts for repeated 4xx/5xx bursts per source.
- **WordPress RCE/account takeover:** Web server/WAF logs for file upload endpoints, unexpected `.php` drops in wp-content/uploads, and abnormal password reset flows (T1190); monitor DNS/HTTP for new outbound traffic from web hosts.
- **Cloud/dev tool abuse (AWS bulletin themes):** CloudTrail + EKS/container runtime logs for unexpected exec into pods, new image pulls, or mutation of “read-only” DB operations (T1059, T1565); flag shell activity on build runners/utility hosts.
- **RMM-phishing “legit tool as trap” trend:** Email security + endpoint for first-time execution/installation of ScreenConnect/ConnectWise/LogMeIn and newly created remote access services (T1566, T1219); require ticket/approval correlation for any RMM installs.

---

### Medium-term follow-ups
- **Patch governance:** Add CVE-2026-85046 (Chrome) and CVE-2026-9586 (Switchvox) to “expedite within 24–48h” SLAs; validate compliance via endpoint management and vuln scanning.
- **CI/CD exposure reduction:** Ensure TeamCity and similar CI tools are not internet-facing; enforce SSO/MFA, IP allowlisting, and secrets rotation playbooks for CI compromise scenarios.
- **Edge appliance posture:** Review SonicWall SMA and other remote-access devices for management plane exposure, WAF/IPS coverage, and log forwarding completeness (many incidents fail due to missing appliance logs).
- **Web/plugin hygiene:** Establish/refresh an allowlist of WordPress plugins for any corporate sites; implement automated plugin inventory + alerting for vulnerable versions.
- **Cloud/tooling supply-chain controls:** For internal use of OSS utilities (including MCP-related tooling), require version pinning, signing/attestation where possible, and rapid deprecation of ad-hoc admin “hotpatch” tools.
- **Playbook refresh:** Update SOC runbooks for “browser zero-day suspected compromise” (rapid triage steps, isolation criteria, credential reset triggers) and for “CI server compromise” (secret rotation + build integrity validation).
